rhs_question_text: A theatre uses a Von Neumann computer to store instructions and ticket sales. Explain the stored-program arrangement of instructions, data and communication buses. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Program instructions and data are held in shared main memory, usually using the same buses/communication pathway between CPU and memory.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for shared memory for code and data and one for shared bus/access or stored-program detail.

rhs_question_text: A computing club compares Harvard with Von Neumann processors. Give one technical architectural feature that differentiates Harvard. [1]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Harvard architecture has separate memory for instructions and data and/or separate instruction and data buses.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for either accurate separation feature.

rhs_question_text: A small community theatre uses a single-core 2.4 GHz CPU with 2 MB cache. State TWO changes to its replacement CPU hardware likely to improve performance. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Increase clock frequency; increase the number of cores; increase cache capacity; processor support for simultaneous multithreading/pipelining may also be relevant.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per distinct improvement expressed relatively (higher, more, larger); a bare change of type with no improvement is insufficient.

rhs_question_text:
A community theatre tracks money raised from ticket purchases using this original Little Man Computer (LMC) listing. Every purchase adds its value to the running sum; a purchase of at least 100 earns an additional 20 bonus units. At the start, sum contains zero. The machine repeatedly asks for another ticket purchase.

START INP
STA ticket
SUB limit
BRP BONUS
REGULAR LDA sum
ADD ticket
STA sum
OUT
BRA START
BONUS LDA sum
ADD ticket
ADD reward
STA sum
OUT
BRA START
limit DAT 100
reward DAT 20
ticket DAT 0
sum DAT 0

The theatre receives tickets with values 10, 50 and 120 in that order. State the three values printed by this program after the respective inputs. [3]
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for each correct cumulative output in the correct position. Retain numeric input sequence and bonus rules for answer comparability.

rhs_question_text: An LMC program has a memory location labelled sum. Write instructions that reset sum to zero and halt. Any valid method is allowed; show all needed DAT constants. [4]
rhs_answer_points_draft:
One possible independent solution:
LDA sum
SUB sum
STA sum
HLT
sum DAT 0
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Four functional criteria from the reference: load a value into accumulator, establish zero, store zero in sum, execute HLT before data. Accept a named zero constant alternative.

rhs_question_text: The theatre's processor can overlap parts of successive instructions. Describe what instruction pipelining does, with reference to Fetch, Decode and Execute. [3]
rhs_answer_points_draft: While one instruction is executed, another may be decoded and a third may be fetched. Different instruction stages overlap, allowing several instructions to be in progress simultaneously.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for overlapping fetch/decode, another for execute being overlapped, and one for concurrent progress of different instructions. Multiple CPU cores are not required.

rhs_question_text: Explain one practical benefit to the theatre of running the repeated ticket-accumulation program on a pipelined CPU. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Greater instruction throughput can complete the same amount of ticket processing in less time, letting the theatre update and display totals more quickly.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for increased instruction throughput / less time per batch, one for specifically applying it to tickets or theatre totals; do not say each individual instruction is necessarily faster.

rhs_question_text: A CPU uses an accumulator as a working register. Describe TWO specific uses of the accumulator during execution. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: It can hold operands/results from the ALU, hold data read from memory and provide a value checked for conditional branching.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per distinct valid role, maximum two.

rhs_question_text: What does the Program Counter hold, and how could its value change when executing ordinary sequential instructions or a branch? [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: The PC stores the address of the next instruction; it normally increments after fetching, but a taken branch/jump loads a target address.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One for next-instruction address; one for increment or branch-related update.

rhs_question_text: Name THREE other CPU registers involved in the FDE cycle, excluding the accumulator and Program Counter. [3]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Any three of MAR (Memory Address Register), MDR (Memory Data Register), CIR (Current Instruction Register), or Index Register (IR), where included.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per distinct correctly identified register, up to three. A name and its abbreviation do not count as two.

rhs_question_text: A charity equips field volunteers with small rechargeable handheld devices. It is choosing between processors based on Reduced Instruction Set Computing (RISC) and Complex Instruction Set Computing (CISC). Discuss both approaches, referring to instruction-set complexity, circuitry, code density, pipelining, energy use and possible application requirements. Recommend a suitable approach for the volunteer devices. [12]
rhs_answer_points_draft: CISC tends to support many complex instructions and sometimes dense code, at the cost of more decoding/control complexity; RISC generally has simpler instructions and regular execution, often beneficial for streamlined pipelines, simpler hardware and power-sensitive devices. Actual efficiency depends on microarchitecture, software, compilers and workload; both may work. Apply the trade-off to portable battery-operated machines and justify a choice.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Teacher-assessed 12-mark levels: high 9–12 thorough accurate, balanced context-sensitive evaluation; middle 5–8 sound but underdeveloped; low 1–4 basic; zero no credit. Compare both designs; do not assert every RISC processor is always faster or lower-power.

Identify the foreign key used to link the two tables AND name the table containing it. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: PlanID in TblMember.

Select a suitable data type for MonthlyCost, which can equal 6.99. [1]

Name the field used to record a customer's advertising consent. [1]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Adverts.

A museum's video service stores two connected tables:
TblMember(MemberID PK, UserName, FirstName, PlanID FK, Adverts BOOLEAN)
TblPlan(PlanID PK, PlanName, MonthlyCost REAL)

Write a complete SQL query that shows ONLY UserName and FirstName of customers who consented to adverts. Join TblMember to TblPlan by PlanID and qualify the join fields. [5]
rhs_answer_points_draft:
SELECT TblMember.UserName, TblMember.FirstName
FROM TblMember
JOIN TblPlan ON TblMember.PlanID = TblPlan.PlanID
WHERE TblMember.Adverts = TRUE;
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Five points: select the two requested fields; correct FROM; valid two-table JOIN; table-qualified join fields; WHERE Adverts=TRUE. A fully working query is required for full marks.

The museum wants new customers to sign up remotely. Recommend one effective DATA CAPTURE method and justify it with TWO scenario-specific benefits. [3]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Online/web registration form can validate entered fields, prevent duplicates and save directly to the central database without staff rekeying.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One for a valid form or equivalent capture method, two for linked advantages. Do not allow barcodes/QR codes as the method of registering a new customer's details.

rhs_question_text: Name TWO different methods or standards for exchanging structured membership data between computer systems. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: CSV, JSON, XML, APIs, EDI, SOAP, SQL export or similar.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per distinct valid method.

rhs_question_text: A museum processes an online membership purchase. Describe the ACID requirement of durability for the completed transaction. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: After COMMIT the data must not be lost, even if power or a server fails.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One for committed data persisting; one for failure protection.

rhs_question_text: State one implementation technique supporting transaction durability. [1]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Store committed information on nonvolatile secondary storage, with appropriate durable logging/flush.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One for persistence beyond volatile RAM.

rhs_question_text: Two sales agents try to update one booking simultaneously. Explain how RECORD LOCKING helps the isolation of transactions. [3]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Concurrent operations should behave as if serial. A record lock restricts conflicting access while a transaction changes a record, preventing lost updates or reads of uncommitted data.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for isolation outcome, one for record exclusive access and one for preventing interleaved conflicting writes/reads.

rhs_question_text: Give one disadvantage of locking database records during busy periods. [1]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Delays while another transaction holds a lock, or deadlock.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for either.

rhs_question_text: A museum streams independent filmmakers' content to paid members. Explain TWO ways copyright protection affects the museum. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Films are generally copyright-protected when created, and the service needs an appropriate licence/authorisation for hosting or streaming; contractual restrictions may apply.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One for owner/protection and one for permission/licensing or appropriate restriction.

rhs_question_text: A museum streams high-definition lecture videos to visitors on different internet connections. Compare LOSSY and LOSSLESS compression, including FIVE technical and viewer-visible consequences for continuous playback. [5]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Lossy encoding discards information irreversibly and may cause quality loss but reduces bitrate/buffering and can adapt to weak connections. Lossless can recreate the original content exactly and preserve fidelity but commonly needs more data/bandwidth and may cause stalls.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per distinct accurate comparison/streaming consequence (max five). Do not award bare 'faster downloads': the context is streaming.

rhs_question_text: A museum represents every lecture with a LectureClip object. Declare a class LectureClip containing PRIVATE title, views and rating. Write a PUBLIC constructor accepting exactly ONE parameter newTitle, setting title from it, views to 0 and rating to 3. [7]
rhs_answer_points_draft:
class LectureClip
  private title
  private views
  private rating
  public procedure new(newTitle)
    title = newTitle
    views = 0
    rating = 3
  endprocedure
endclass
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Seven mark points: class name, three attributes, PRIVATE visibility, public constructor, one data parameter, title initialisation, views=0 and rating=3 together. Equivalent correct OOP syntax accepted.

rhs_question_text: Write a PUBLIC zero-parameter method increaseViews() for LectureClip that adds one to its existing private views attribute. [2]
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One for public method, one for updating views by exactly one.

rhs_question_text: An airport's access system records a code as hexadecimal B7E. Write that value as a twelve-bit binary number. [1]
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for all twelve bits correct; keep the exact source hexadecimal value.

rhs_question_text: A survey sensor stores an integer as sign-and-magnitude bits 110010101. Convert it to denary. [1]
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for negative 149, reflecting sign bit 1 and magnitude 149.

rhs_question_text: A controller stores signed eight-bit two's-complement values. Subtract 0011 0100 from 0110 1101, showing BINARY working and giving the eight-bit result. [3]
rhs_answer_points_draft: 0110 1101 − 0011 0100 = 0011 1001. Equivalent addition of the two's-complement negative subtrahend is valid.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for high nibble 0011, one for low nibble 1001, one for clearly shown binary carry/borrow or two's complement working. Denary-only working is not awarded method credit.

rhs_question_text: A water-level device reads a signed binary floating-point pattern 1010 1110 with four-bit two's-complement fractional mantissa and four-bit two's-complement exponent. The point is immediately after the sign bit. Calculate its denary value with working. [4]
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Four source-aligned working points: exponent -2; signed mantissa -0.75 / binary-point movement; signed extension or shift; correct -0.1875.

rhs_question_text:
For each six-bit two's-complement mantissa and three-bit two's-complement exponent below, write NORMALISED or NOT NORMALISED. A normalised mantissa has different first two bits. [4]
(a) 010101 100
(b) 110101 111
(c) 011010 010
(d) 101010 110
rhs_answer_points_draft: (a) normalised; (b) not normalised; (c) normalised; (d) normalised.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per exact classification; do not credit contradictory dual selections.

rhs_question_text: A public transport authority plans to use machine learning to assess passenger complaints. The system's developers have chosen the training examples and labelling rules. Discuss whether the resulting AI could learn biases, explain how AI and machine learning differ, provide relevant discrimination examples, and evaluate practical safeguards and human oversight. [9]
rhs_answer_points_draft: AI systems undertake tasks requiring human-like judgement; machine learning adjusts performance from examples. Bias may enter via unrepresentative or historically biased training data, labels, design choices and evaluation metrics. Mitigate with representative audited data, tests across populations, diverse design scrutiny, transparency, appeal processes and regular monitoring. Evaluate residual limitations and human oversight.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Nine-mark holistic assessment, 7–9 thorough balanced applied evaluation, 4–6 sound but incomplete, 1–3 basic, 0 none. Do not treat bigger datasets alone as guaranteeing fairness.

rhs_question_text:
A theatre tracks rehearsal scores using this original pseudocode:
function seriesTotal(left,right)
  answer = 0
  do
    answer = answer + left + right
    left = left - 10
    right = right - 10
  until left < 0
  return answer
endfunction

rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for 40.

rhs_question_text: Describe the function of a translator before a computer executes high-level source code. [1]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Converts high-level/assembly source into machine or lower-level code.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for translating to lower-level or machine instructions.

rhs_question_text: Compare compiler and interpreter behaviour in TWO distinct paired ways. [4]
rhs_answer_points_draft: A compiler typically translates a whole program before it runs; an interpreter processes statements at runtime. A compiled executable can be reused without retranslation, while interpreted source usually needs its runtime again. Error reporting and source visibility are other valid paired differences.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Two marks per paired comparison of the SAME feature, up to four.

rhs_question_text: A pupil classifies compiler activities using L for lexical analysis, S for syntax analysis and G for code generation. Give the correct stage letter for: 1 removing comments; 2 creating keyword tokens; 3 generating object code; 4 entering identifiers in a symbol table; 5 constructing an abstract syntax tree. [5]
rhs_answer_points_draft: L, L, G, L, S.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per correct stage, with exactly one selection per description.

rhs_question_text: A games developer runs an optimisation pass on translated code. Explain TWO possible goals of this process. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Reduce execution time or instruction count; reduce memory and other resource use without changing program behaviour.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for time/efficiency goal, one for resource/memory goal.

rhs_question_text:
Complete three gaps in this original routine which counts uppercase ASCII letters, codes 65 through 90. [3]
function upperCount(message)
  total = 0
  for index = 0 to message.length - 1
    character = message[index]
    if asc(character) >= 65 ______ then
      total = ______
    endif
  next index
  return ______
endfunction
rhs_answer_points_draft: In order: and asc(character) <= 90; total + 1; total.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per correct range check, counter increment and returned counter.

rhs_question_text: Give one characteristic ASCII and Unicode have in common. [1]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Both assign numeric codes to characters.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One for describing a shared character-encoding purpose.

rhs_question_text: Explain TWO differences between ASCII and Unicode. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: ASCII uses a smaller basic character repertoire and 7-bit codes; Unicode covers many world scripts and symbols, with variable-length UTF encodings such as UTF-8.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per fully paired distinction, such as character range and possible bit representation.

rhs_question_text: A library commissions a complex inventory application whose requirements may change after early testing. Compare the SPIRAL development model with WATERFALL. Evaluate stages, risk review, feedback, cost and project suitability. [9]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Waterfall has sequential, planned analysis/design/implementation/testing stages suited to stable agreed requirements, with costly late changes. Spiral repeats objective-setting, risk analysis, prototype development and evaluation, supporting early feedback and change at higher management cost. Justify the choice for evolving library requirements.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Teacher-assessed 9-mark holistic bands: 7–9 thorough balanced applied argument, 4–6 sound, 1–3 basic, 0 none. No keyword auto-grading.

rhs_question_text: Why is FIRST COME FIRST SERVED suitable for a shared printer where all submitted jobs have equal priority? [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Each job has equal priority; the printer takes jobs in arrival order, a FIFO queue.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One for equal priority, one for print in arrival order.

rhs_question_text: Explain how ROUND ROBIN scheduling keeps a browser, ticket app and editor responsive on one processor. [3]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Each ready process receives a time quantum; unfinished work returns to the ready queue; the scheduler cycles between them to make progress on multiple jobs.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One for time slicing, one for repeated cycling/requeue, one for multitasking responsiveness.

rhs_question_text: Give a CPU scheduling method other than FCFS or Round Robin, and explain its selection rule. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Shortest Job First chooses the job with shortest expected run duration; Shortest Remaining Time favours shortest remaining job with preemption; multi-level feedback schedules across changing-priority queues.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One for valid different method, one for characteristic operation.

rhs_question_text: A school app exchanges PRIVATE online messages using TCP/IP. Describe FIVE application-layer operations involved in sending or receiving encrypted messages. [5]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Choose a service-appropriate secure protocol such as HTTPS for web-based messaging; prepare message/application data; apply encryption via the app security protocol; pass outgoing data to transport; receive data from transport, decrypt as required and present content.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Up to five distinct appropriate application-layer steps. Do not list HTTP as a secure protocol in this scenario.

rhs_question_text: State TWO operations handled at TCP/IP's LINK layer as the messages cross the school's Wi-Fi network. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Encapsulate data in local frames with MAC addressing and transmit frames over the local wireless link; reverse when receiving.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One for framing or MAC addresses, one for sending/receiving through link or transferring back to internet layer.
